sense.text:
“And I saw an angel come down from heaven, having the key of the bottomless pit and a great chain in his hand”: this great chain that binds Satan is a twofold scripture. Not all scriptures have a twofold meaning; some do, some do not, some have more than two. The first understanding is the spiritual one: the spirits are bound captive for an allotted time. Then there is the literal one: the children of the devil on this earth are bound. “And he laid hold on the dragon, that old serpent, which is the Devil, and Satan, and bound him a thousand years”: the spiritual demons are bound, and the literal demons on this earth are bound for a thousand years.

This bottomless pit is Europe. Gog and Magog are the areas of Russia and Scythia around the Caucasus mountains. They came from those mountains, and a lot of them are going right back there again. That is the bottomless pit.

“And cast him into the bottomless pit, and shut him up, and set a seal upon him”: when Christ died and was put in a tomb, the seal was put on the tomb so that nobody would take the body. When the king puts a seal, it is his signet, so you know it is of the king and you don’t mess with it. “That he should deceive the nations no more, till the thousand years should be fulfilled: and after that he must be loosed a little season.”

precepts.why: The scriptures can be twofold: “And that he would shew thee the secrets of wisdom, that they are double to that which is!”

The spiritual understanding, Legion. “Art thou come hither to torment us before the time?”: there is an allotted time for spiritual binding, for the spirits to be bound captive. And look how wicked people are: Christ healed two possessed with devils that tormented the whole city, and “they besought him that he would depart out of their coasts.”
The literal meaning, the binding of men: “To bind their kings with chains, and their nobles with fetters of iron.”

“And the great dragon was cast out, that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan, which deceiveth the whole world”: also a twofold scripture. It goes into the spiritual demons, but it also goes into the children of Satan.

“In this the children of God are manifest, and the children of the devil”: in this earth you have the children of God and the children of the devil. A black man or woman who is wicked is acting like the devil, but they can do what other nations can’t do: repent.

The law of sacrifice was instituted way before Moses; it was reinforced with Moses but instituted here. “If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted?”: if you obey my commandments, won’t you be accepted? “And if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door. And unto thee shall be his desire, and thou shalt rule over him”: your desire shall be to Satan and Satan shall rule over you; you will be a child of the devil. The lineage of Cain, before the flood, and then the entire line of Esau, are the literal children of the devil. When we do wrong we act like the children of the devil, because we aren’t keeping the commandments, but we are truly the sons and daughters of God. The white man is the literal children of the devil.

“The earth shall reel to and fro like a drunkard”: that is when the second coming of the Lord and nuclear destruction hit this earth. “And it shall fall, and not rise again”: those old inhabitants will not rise again. “The Lord shall punish the host of the high ones that are on high”: punishing the white man, on high above all nations. “And they shall be gathered together, as prisoners are gathered in the pit”: that is the bottomless pit. “And shall be shut up in the prison”: that is captivity. “And after many days shall they be visited”: after a thousand years they shall be visited again.

sense.text:
“And I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them”: there is a lot of meat on this verse. The judgment given to the saints is power. If somebody told you to go take over all of New York City, you would need power; you aren’t going to Japan to say a thing without power.

“And which had not worshipped the beast, neither his image, neither had received his mark upon their foreheads, or in their hands”: the beast is the white man; the image is the Christian church system; the mark is their political and economic policies.

“And they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years”: the old teaching was that this reign was the Dark Ages. That is not right, because during the Dark Ages we were wicked as hell. That was us in the Catholic Church having reign and rule over the people, holding people’s confessions over them to control them. Reigning with Christ is the kingdom to come.

precepts.why: “In the regeneration when the Son of man shall sit in the throne of his glory”: that is the kingdom of heaven on earth. “Ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel”: the twelve are the top of the 144,000; they are the leaders.
“And judgment was given to the saints of the most High; and the time came that the saints possessed the kingdom”: what kind of judgment do we need to take the kingdom? Power.

“Do ye not know that the saints shall judge the world?”: to judge the world you need power. Paul was reminding the Israelites in Corinth, who were scared to judge a situation: “Are ye unworthy to judge the smallest matters?” People say you are not supposed to judge; that’s a lie. We judge the small matters amongst us; murder, a stolen car, rape are outside our jurisdiction today. “Know ye not that we shall judge angels?”: this is not Michael, Gabriel and Uriel up in the heavens. The word angels simply means messengers. This is why the ranking system will be enforced all over again: captains and officers set over men, judging those men, meaning commanding them.

“And the nations were angry”: you think the nations will be happy when Christ returns? “And that thou shouldest give reward unto thy servants the prophets, and to the saints”: the reward we get is power.

For those who say rank is evil. “And purely purge away thy dross, and take away all thy tin”: when you purge gold you take out the dross and the tin, all the unnatural elements; God will purge our sin. “And I will restore thy judges as at the first, and thy counsellors as at the beginning.”

What “as at the first” means: “Judges and officers shalt thou make thee in all thy gates, which the Lord thy God giveth thee, throughout thy tribes: and they shall judge the people with just judgment.” God is going to restore that to us; we go right back to that system again.

It even goes for today. Go to any other nation and you see order, structure, organization. “That thou shouldest set in order the things that are wanting, and ordain elders in every city”: elders are officers, judges, counsellors. The ranking system.

Corinth was a troublesome camp. “If then ye have judgments of things pertaining to this life, set them to judge who are least esteemed in the church. I speak to your shame”: if you older brothers won’t judge, then set up the young men that just came in. “Is it so, that there is not a wise man among you? no, not one that shall be able to judge between his brethren?”

Rank in the kingdom: “I will also make thy officers peace, and thine exactors righteousness.” That goes right back to Deuteronomy 16:18 and Isaiah 1. Don’t ever think there will be no rank in the kingdom and we are all equal; there must be order. Without order you have chaos.
Reigning with Christ for a thousand years kills the Dark Ages thought: “But the saints of the most High shall take the kingdom, and possess the kingdom for ever, even for ever and ever.”

“And the kingdom and dominion, and the greatness of the kingdom under the whole heaven”: the whole planet earth “shall be given to the people of the saints of the most High.” “And all dominions shall serve and obey him”: that him is Christ. “Hitherto is the end of the matter”: this is what the whole Bible is about. God’s plan from the beginning was to give the planet back to the saints, the Israelites. Equality with all nations is what you learned in democracy, not what the Bible says.

“If the world now be made for our sakes, why do we not possess an inheritance with the world? how long shall this endure?”: the world was made for the Israelites, not for all nations to rule. Ezra asked how long, and Daniel answered: the kingdom shall be given to the saints.

What the world will look like when we reign: “Moreover the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun, and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold.” “In the day that the Lord bindeth up the breach of his people”: when he brings back the twelve tribes of Israel.

“The mountain of the Lord’s house shall be established in the top of the mountains”: the kingdom will be literally at the top of the highest mountain. You will always look up to Jerusalem; that is literal and spiritual. We will be the top of all governments on the earth. “For out of Zion shall go forth the law”: the law is what will be taught throughout the earth. The law is the true religion; it always has been and always will be.

“The wolf also shall dwell with the lamb, and the leopard shall lie down with the kid”: what wolves and leopards do to lambs and kids is eat them, but not during the thousand-year reign. “And the lion shall eat straw like the ox.” “For the earth shall be full of the knowledge of the Lord, as the waters cover the sea”: when the Lord goes forth he will put a spirit on everything to return to the way it was supposed to be. His word, his laws, have power, and as we apply the laws they bring forth change in our lives and those around us.

Why the lion eats straw: “And to every beast of the earth, and to every fowl of the air, and to every thing that creepeth upon the earth, wherein there is life, I have given every green herb for meat.” In the beginning no animal ate another animal. That is why the lions didn’t attack the other animals on Noah’s ark.

sense.text:
“But the rest of the dead lived not again until the thousand years were finished”: we have learned that you do come back. Some camps say you can be an adulterer, a thief, a liar, a drug addict, die in your sin and inherit the kingdom. Then why discipline our lives? Why read the Bible?

The generation Christ spoke of is the generation in the last days before his return; that same wicked group that rejected him is coming back. Those of the two parts that are put to death here, that reject the Lord, are not coming back in the kingdom as children: “the rest of the dead lived not again until the thousand years were finished.”

precepts.why: “But the blasphemy against the Holy Ghost shall not be forgiven unto men”: blasphemy against the Holy Ghost is when you learn the law and reject it. “Neither in this world, neither in the world to come”: do not think you will live like the devil and inherit the kingdom.

“For it is impossible for those who were once enlightened, and have tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Ghost”: if you fall out of this truth and follow the heretics twisting God’s law, it is impossible “to renew them again unto repentance.” You are wasting your breath praying they repent; you will see them go into more and more heresies. “And put him to an open shame”: they went right back to their vomit.

The Church only knows the Holy Ghost as spiritual power, healing the sick. That is the power aspect, but the initial aspect is explained here: “Ye do always resist the Holy Ghost: as your fathers did, so do ye.” “Who have received the law by the disposition of angels, and have not kept it”: what they were resisting was the law of God.

“Cast me not away from thy presence; and take not thy holy spirit from me”: the Holy Spirit is the Holy Ghost, the same thing. Did David have spiritual power? No. He prayed, don’t take that spirit of understanding from me. It refers to the law.

People do come back. Do you think the slave owners who raped slaves just died and got away scot free? Nobody gets away with nothing with our Lord. “And they also which pierced him”: those that pierced him did so over 2,000 years ago. How will they see him if they don’t come back? They will be back alive with their minds open.

“Let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me”: that requires one word, discipline. Could have, should have, would have: that is Satan. You could have been all that, but the things you would have had to do are where the sin begins. “For whosoever will save his life shall lose it”: losing your life doesn’t mean suicide; it means losing the path you were gunning for, and following Christ. “For what is a man advantaged, if he gain the whole world, and lose himself, or be cast away?” Satan offered Christ all the kingdoms of the world if he would worship him, and he says the same to us. “There be some standing here, which shall not taste of death, till they see the kingdom of God”: they died and are gone, so they are coming back, and when the Lord returns they will see him with their own eyes and meet their ultimate death and damnation. There are levels in this book.

“That in all the land”: singular, one particular land, Babylon the great. “Two parts therein shall be cut off and die”: two parts amongst the Israelites. “And I will bring the third part through the fire”: that is twofold, the nuclear destruction as well as your own fire and hell in your personal life. “And will refine them as silver is refined.”

For your mothers, fathers, sisters, brothers and kids who hear the truth and reject it: they fall into those two parts. “And for this cause God shall send them strong delusion, that they should believe a lie: that they all might be damned who believed not the truth, but had pleasure in unrighteousness”: pleasure in sin, in the Catholic Church, the Christian church. If she heard the truth and rejected it and died, I can’t help her and you can’t help her.

For those who never heard, like a grandmother who died years ago: “I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I will have compassion.” That compassion goes for those who did not hear the truth; the Bible makes it clear that those who heard it and rejected it are damned.

sense.text: “This is the first resurrection”: write this down, it is of those that take part in verse 4, the souls that had not worshipped the beast, “and they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years.”

“Blessed and holy is he that hath part in the first resurrection: on such the second death hath no power”: everybody in here wants to be part of the first resurrection. “But they shall be priests of God and of Christ, and shall reign with him a thousand years.”

precepts.why: The first resurrection. “Concerning them which are asleep”: those that died in this truth. “That ye sorrow not, even as others which have no hope”: like your grandmother who loved the picture of a white man on the wall; she loved the image of the beast. “We which are alive and remain unto the coming of the Lord shall not prevent them which are asleep”: Paul is saying about himself, I am going to be there; he sees something in the spirit. “And the dead in Christ shall rise first”: that is the first resurrection. “Wherefore comfort one another with these words”: we have to believe we will see them again. If all those prophecies about slavery came to pass, this one about the resurrection will too.
“Wheresoever thou findest the dead, take them and bury them, and I will give thee the first place in my resurrection.”

The woman with the seven sons; one of the sons, ready to die, speaking to a Greek: “It is good, being put to death by men, to look for hope from God to be raised up again by him”: that is the first resurrection. “As for thee, thou shalt have no resurrection to life”: the rest of the dead lived not again till the thousand years were finished.

“All that are in the graves shall hear his voice”: those that die will hear the voice of the Lord when he returns. “They that have done evil, unto the resurrection of damnation”: people who died thinking they got away with all that evil will be raised up, put to death and damned forever. That is why we can’t play in this truth.

Meditate on scriptures like this before you do some evil. “And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life”: that is the first resurrection. “And some to shame and everlasting contempt”: that is damnation.

Moses told us about this, and it is twofold: “And ye shall be unto me a kingdom of priests, and an holy nation.” You think of the Levites, but Moses was talking about the kingdom to come: all you men that make it shall be priests of God.
Here’s the proof: “And hath made us kings and priests unto God and his Father.” That is what Moses was talking about.

“But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people.” Peter was talking to his generation, and they were all put to death in 70 AD; they were at the beginning stages, but this goes for us today in the last days, under America. “Which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God”: they changed all our identities and said you are no people, you are three fifths of a man. Now we are awake; we are the Israelites, the sons of God.

sense.text: “And when the thousand years are expired, Satan shall be loosed out of his prison”: the story doesn’t end there. Even on the other side, things must come to pass; the difference is that in the kingdom our minds will be open to see and comprehend more.

“And shall go out to deceive the nations which are in the four quarters of the earth”: just like the binding, the loosing is twofold. It goes for the physical, men released from captivity, and for Satan the spiritual demon. “Gog and Magog, to gather them together to battle: the number of whom is as the sand of the sea.” The Christian commentaries tell you Ezekiel 38 is for now, but Revelation 20 tells you it is after the thousand-year reign of Christ.

“And they went up on the breadth of the earth, and compassed the camp of the saints about, and the beloved city”: the mountain of the Lord’s house is at the top of the mountains, and these nations will come around the camp of Israel to destroy us. “And fire came down from God out of heaven, and devoured them.”

precepts.why: “And shall be shut up in the prison, and after many days shall they be visited”: after the thousand years Satan shall be loosed.

“After many days thou shalt be visited”: saying the same thing. “Thou shalt come into the land that is brought back from the sword, and is gathered out of many people, against the mountains of Israel”: once they are loosed they will come against the land of Israel, gathered back. “And they shall dwell safely all of them”: the Israelites there will be dwelling safely, and then these nations come against us.

“Son of man, set thy face against Gog, the land of Magog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal.” “Persia, Ethiopia, and Libya with them.” “And many people with thee”: when these nations are released the party isn’t over. We will be the top nation on the planet, and they will be jealous and say they have to destroy us again.
Ezekiel 39 picks up where Ezekiel 38 ends: “And I will send a fire on Magog, and among them that dwell carelessly in the isles: and they shall know that I am the Lord.”

The devil cast into the lake of fire is the spiritual demon, but it also goes with your friendly neighborhood white man. You have been conditioned to think you need them. “And the house of Jacob shall be a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau for stubble.” “And there shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau; for the Lord hath spoken it.” We are just reading the Bible.

sense.text:
“And the devil that deceived them was cast into the lake of fire and brimstone, where the beast and the false prophet are”: the beast and the false prophet were already cast into the lake of fire before the thousand-year reign of Christ. They were destroyed at Christ’s coming, so John says they are already there. “And shall be tormented day and night for ever and ever”: you are not escaping.

Where is the false prophet in verse 4? It doesn’t use the words false prophet: the false prophet is the image that people worship.

precepts.why: “And I saw the beast”: the beast is the European Union. “And the beast was taken, and with him the false prophet that wrought miracles before him”: those miracles are their science, space, technology, DNA, cloning and blending. “These both were cast alive into a lake of fire burning with brimstone”: that is when the nuclear bombs hit and the third world war kicks off; they will be destroyed.

“That they should make an image to the beast.” “That the image of the beast should both speak, and cause that as many as would not worship the image of the beast should be killed”: what do people do with this image? Worship it. The false prophet that wrought miracles in Revelation 19:20 is this image.
“Take heed that no man deceive you. For many shall come in my name, saying, I am Christ; and shall deceive many”: that is the image the world would worship.

“And it was given unto him to make war with the saints, and to overcome them”: the white man made war with the saints, the twelve tribes, and Esau overcame us. “And power was given him over all kindreds, and tongues, and nations”: he took over everything, like the British trying to take over China. “And all that dwell upon the earth shall worship him”: everybody is worshipping the white man.

sense.text: “And I saw a great white throne, and him that sat on it, from whose face the earth and the heaven fled away”: when the Ancient of days comes on the scene, nobody has anything to say. The earth means everybody on it, and the heaven means the angels. Like when the king comes to the throne and everybody bows and it is quiet: when the Father comes, everybody shuts up. “And there was found no place for them.”

“And I saw the dead, small and great, stand before God”: this is the final judgment, from the smallest that were born on earth to the greatest people ever known. “And the books were opened”: notice, books, plural. There will be several books. We will be judged on what we have studied and learned according to scripture, and that will be compared with the book on you: on this date you did this, here is what the scripture says about that. It says books because that is how we see things, but this is the spirit world; your life will be opened, and there will be no arguing.

The difference between verse 6 and verse 12: those in verse 6, who make the first resurrection, are keeping the laws. Verse 12 is everybody on the planet, and they are not keeping the laws.

precepts.why: Why a great white throne: “And the Ancient of days did sit, whose garment was white as snow”: this is the Father. To have a garment you have to have a body to put the clothing on. “And the hair of his head like the pure wool”: proving that God is a black man. “His throne was like the fiery flame, and his wheels as burning fire”: those were chariots.

“Take heed that ye despise not one of these little ones”: the little ones are those that have repented in Christ. “That in heaven their angels do always behold the face of my Father which is in heaven”: their, possessive. Every one of us has an angel who records what we do and reports to the Father. Esau calls it a guardian angel, and they got that from the Bible. That is rank, order, structure.

“Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man”: you don’t need a motivational speaker to tell you the purpose of man. “For God shall bring every work into judgment, with every secret thing, whether it be good, or whether it be evil”: every secret thing. What we show each other is only what we want to show; everybody in here has another side.
“For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ; that every one may receive the things done in his body, according to that he hath done, whether it be good or bad.”

“My little children, let us not love in word, neither in tongue; but in deed and in truth”: that is why it is very important to love our neighbour as ourselves. We will be judged on what we do, good or bad, and every secret thing.

sense.text: “And the sea gave up the dead which were in it”: you think your family member got away because you cremated them and scattered their ashes in the sea? They are not escaping this judgment; that body will be reformed and stand before the God of heaven and earth. “And death and hell delivered up the dead which were in them”: death and hell refer to the ground, those buried in the earth, those burned, those covered by rocks or mudslides. Their bodies will be reformed and brought before the Lord. “And they were judged every man according to their works.”

“And death and hell were cast into the lake of fire”: this is when death ends. “This is the second death.” Those that make the first resurrection will not have to go through verse 11 down; on such the second death hath no power. You are exempt from this final judgment. The second death is when everyone that ever lived is judged, except those that made the first resurrection, and after that judgment death and hell are finished.

Is death ended right away? For the elect who make the first resurrection, yes. For the rest of the people born into the earth, there will still be death. As soon as Christ returns, the whole earth does not submit; the only ones that will submit are the elect. The nations must be subdued, and that takes time, just like when we had to take down the land of Canaan. Moses told Gad and Reuben they could have their inheritance first, but not to inhabit it till they helped their brothers take down theirs. It will be the same way again: ambassadors will be sent to nations with an ultimatum to submit to the King of kings, and men will be sent to take them down.

precepts.why: “But every man in his own order”: there is no equality with God; there will be order. “Christ the firstfruits”: he is the King, the first. “When he shall have delivered up the kingdom to God, even the Father”: Christ and the heavenly Father are not the same. “When he shall have put down all rule and all authority and power”: all nations will be under submission, and that will take time.
Some of us think that as soon as Christ returns the whole earth submits. “And they repented not to give him glory.” “And repented not of their deeds”: they are not changing their ways.
If all nations submit when Christ returns, why do we need this? “But the saints of the most High shall take the kingdom”: we are not going to ask for anything; we are going to take it.
“And I will lay my vengeance upon Edom by the hand of my people Israel”: subduing this nation, binding them, putting them in the bottomless pit, those Caucasus mountains, takes time.

“Turn you to the strong hold, ye prisoners of hope”: we are the prisoners, and our hope is to return to greatness, to who we are and always have been meant to be. “Even to day do I declare that I will render double unto thee”: all that we suffered. “When I have bent Judah for me, filled the bow with Ephraim”: the southern and northern kingdoms like a weapon of war. “And raised up thy sons, O Zion, against thy sons, O Greece”: the sons of Greece are your friendly neighborhood white man. “And the Lord shall be seen over them”: that is on the other side, with the King of kings. “And subdue with sling stones.” “For they shall be as the stones of a crown, lifted up as an ensign upon his land.”

When we got to the promised land, ten of the spies said they are giants; Caleb and Joshua said we can overcome them. It is the same again: we have to subdue the earth. “And the remnant of Jacob shall be among the Gentiles in the midst of many people”: that is the planet earth. “As a young lion among the flocks of sheep”: not an old lion, a young lion in his prime. “Who, if he go through, both treadeth down, and teareth in pieces, and none can deliver.”

“Have thou authority over ten cities”: it doesn’t say where the ten cities are; they can be anywhere on the earth. And those cities won’t want to hear a thing you say: you will have to subdue them and enforce God’s laws. The white man, when he conquered us, changed our language and taught us marriage, what to eat and what not to eat; we have to undo everything that has been instituted in the earth. One city like New York has over eight million people, and we must teach them all what to eat, what holidays to keep, how to dress modestly.

“And their seed shall be known among the Gentiles, and their offspring among the people: all that see them shall acknowledge them, that they are the seed which the Lord hath blessed”: imagine the nations all knowing your children by name and moving out of their way. Today they acknowledge our kids through the school-to-prison pipeline, but on that day it will be different.

“And thy seed shall inherit the Gentiles, and make the desolate cities to be inhabited”: our children will own the nations. “For thou shalt not be put to shame”: if you believe this book you will never be ashamed. “For thou shalt forget the shame of thy youth”: the shame of our youth is what we are going through now. “And shalt not remember the reproach of thy widowhood any more.”

“For he must reign, till he hath put all enemies under his feet. The last enemy that shall be destroyed is death.” “It is manifest that he is excepted, which did put all things under him”: he puts everything under his feet except the Father. “Then shall the Son also himself be subject unto him that put all things under him, that God may be all in all”: Christ is the reigning God on the planet earth, and then he submits everything to the heavenly Father. When you read the scriptures, that is Christ all through there with us.

“And the government shall be upon his shoulder”: God is setting up a government under Christ, with the twelve, and under them the rest of the 144,000. “And his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace”: one of his names is the everlasting Father. When you thought you were dealing with the Father throughout the scriptures, most of it is Christ.

sense.text: “And whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire”: that verse speaks volumes. You want to know what will happen to these people: you just read it. Who is in the book of life? Israel, the elect of Israel. If your name isn’t in the book of life, you are cast in and destroyed. Bye-bye, nations. Everything was made for us: the people on the planet, the earth itself.

precepts.why: Who is in the book of life: “And at that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince which standeth for the children of thy people.” “And at that time thy people shall be delivered, every one that shall be found written in the book.”

sense.text: Baptism. Nobody ever said getting dipped in water is a sin; what we say is that it is symbolic. Today people want a Shazam effect: they don’t want the discipline of changing their life; they would rather be dipped in some pool water and come up a changed man or woman. It doesn’t happen like that; you are still as wicked as before you went in the water. “The like figure whereunto even baptism doth also now save us”: Peter reveals that baptism does save you. “Not the putting away of the filth of the flesh”: water is what takes the filth from your flesh, and that type of baptism does not save you. “But the answer of a good conscience toward God”: our conscience is found in our mind, and we have a good conscience when we are keeping the commandments in Christ.

precepts.why: Water was used symbolically, and John’s baptism was based on scriptures like this: “Wash you, make you clean; put away the evil of your doings.” That is what it symbolized.
“For though thou wash thee with nitre, and take thee much soap, yet thine iniquity is marked before me, saith the Lord God”: all that washing makes no change on your inside.

“And were baptized of him in Jordan, confessing their sins”: in the time of John the Baptist they were sincere and confessed their sins. Find anybody on Facebook or YouTube getting dipped in water confessing their sins; all you see is the dip. That is still not following the scriptures.

sense.text: Family members who are still alive and have rejected the truth: don’t count them out yet. Remember the apostle Paul did not accept the gospel when he first heard it. They are counted out when they die; while they are still alive there is still hope. Women came into the truth whose husbands did not believe, and Peter’s answer goes for your parents too. “Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands; that, if any obey not the word, they also may without the word be won by the conversation of the wives”: without the word, meaning they don’t know the word.

“While they behold your chaste conversation coupled with fear”: the way you conduct yourself. The same way Peter instructed the wives to deal with unbelieving husbands, you brothers and sisters with unbelieving parents win them by your conversation coupled with fear.

precepts.why: A young man once cursed out his parents to go to Passover and was put to death in a car accident on the way back; the last thing his parents heard from him was curses. “Honour thy father with thy whole heart, and forget not the sorrows of thy mother. Remember that thou wast begotten of them; and how canst thou recompense them the things that they have done for thee?” There is no way you can pay your parents back; all you can do is give glory to the Lord for them.
